subject: Vocabulary
description: Common Greek/Latin prefixes — anti, ante, ad, con, dis, mis, sub, super, trans

questions.explanation: ANTE- = before. Examples: ANTECHAMBER (room before main chamber), ANTEDATE (before a date), ANTEROOM, ANTEBELLUM (pre-war). DON'T confuse with ANTI- (against): antithesis, antibody, antigravity. POST- = after. SUB- = under. ANTE comes from Latin; ANTI from Greek.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.explanation: MIS- = wrongly, badly. Examples: MISUNDERSTAND (understand wrongly), MISUSE, MISCALCULATE, MISBEHAVE, MISPRONOUNCE. Old English origin. Distractors are different prefixes: MULTI- (many), SEMI- (half), CO-/COM-/CON- (together).
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.explanation: TRANS- = across, through, beyond. Latin origin. Examples: TRANSPORT (carry across), TRANSCONTINENTAL (across a continent), TRANSFER, TRANSPLANT, TRANSPARENT (light passes through), TRANSLATE (carry meaning across languages). SUPER- = above. SUB- = under. MULTI- = many.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: The prefix DIS- (as in 'disagree', 'dishonest') typically means:

options.option_text: Not, opposite of, or apart from

questions.explanation: DIS- = not, opposite of, or apart. Examples: DISAGREE, DISHONEST, DISCOURAGE, DISCONNECT, DISLIKE, DISAPPEAR. Latin origin. Same family: UN- (English; unhappy, undo), IN-/IM- (Latin; incomplete, impossible), NON- (nonexistent). Distractor 1 BI- (twice). Distractor 3 SUB- (under). Distractor 4 SEMI- (half).
questions.subject: Vocabulary

options.option_text: Two or double (like the prefix bi-)
Through or across (like the prefix trans-)

questions.explanation: CIRCUM- = around. Latin 'circum' (around). Examples: CIRCUMNAVIGATE (sail around), CIRCUMFERENCE (boundary around a circle), CIRCUMSPECT (literally 'looking around' → cautious), CIRCUMVENT (go around an obstacle), CIRCUMSCRIBE (draw a line around → limit). Same root as 'circle'. Distractor 1 INTRA-. Distractor 3 BI-. Distractor 4 TRANS-.

options.option_text: Below the normal level (like prefix hypo-)
Above the normal level, excessive level
Equal to a baseline (like prefix equi-)
Of the self or own (like the prefix auto-)

questions.explanation: HYPER- = above, excessive. Greek origin. Examples: HYPERTENSION (high BP), HYPERACTIVE, HYPERSONIC (>5× speed of sound), HYPERBOLE (extreme exaggeration). DISTINGUISHED from HYPO- = below, deficient: HYPOTENSION (low BP), HYPOTHERMIA, HYPOTHESIS. Both Greek; one letter difference makes them opposite. Distractor 3 EQUI-. Distractor 4 AUTO-.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.explanation: POST- = after. Latin origin. Examples: POSTPONE (delay to a later time), POSTWAR (after the war), POST-MORTEM (after death; medical examination), POSTGRADUATE, POSTSCRIPT. Antonym prefix: PRE- = before. Distractor 1 PRE-. Distractor 3 EX-. Distractor 4 INTRA-/IN-.
